reason: The picture shows the turning sensor cells at the base of a fluid-filled loop, matching the first goal.
expectation: The cells will detect movement of fluid as the head starts turning.

effect: The turning sensors are built; fluid movement bends them and changes a nerve signal.
reaction: The picture makes the connection between turning and the signal clearer.
reason: The mineral weights sit above the tilt sensor cells in the pictures, matching the goal of building weighted tilt sensors.
expectation: The weights will help the jelly layer move and bend the sensors when the head tilts.

effect: The weighted sensors are built, and the picture shows how their shifting layer bends hairs during tilt or a change in straight-line movement.
reaction: The weights' purpose is clearer now.
reason: Both types of sensor need the balance nerves to send information toward the brain. I'll connect the turning sensors first.
expectation: The turning sensors will connect to a nerve route toward the brain.

alternatives.reason: The tilt sensors also need a route to the brain.

effect: The two sensor types had to be combined into balance organs before connecting their nerve route.
reaction: I expected to connect the turning sensors directly, so the required pairing surprised me.
reason: The balance nerves are pictured connecting both kinds of sensor to the brain, so they should fit the combined organs.
expectation: The balance organs will have a nerve route carrying their signals toward the brain.

effect: The balance organs cannot currently be combined, so I need another route toward connecting the sensors.
reaction: I'm unsure why the nerve connection did not work yet.
reason: Inspecting the balance nerves should reveal what they can connect to now, rather than guessing another prerequisite.
expectation: The compatibility list will show an available connection for the balance nerves.

effect: The balance nerves joined the eye and posture routes automatically, completing the link and revealing a goal to connect it to the body.
reaction: The compatibility hint clarified the required order, which wasn't obvious to me.
reason: The new goal calls for the body to respond, so I'll connect it to the balance response routes.
expectation: The body will gain the nerve routes for responding to head movement.

alternatives.reason: The body also needs the inner-ear sensors, but the new goal points toward the response routes.

effect: The body now has balance response routes, but the sensors remain unconnected.
reaction: The pale spaces make the remaining connection clear.
reason: The balance organs contain the sensors that fit the unconnected spaces beside the ears.
expectation: The sensors will connect to the body's balance routes, allowing it to respond to head movement.

effect: Connecting the balance organs completed the body’s response: the picture shows the eyes countering a head turn and the body adjusting posture. Vision and signals from muscles and joints also help.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate sensors and routes lead to a visible response.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the sensors to the body was most worthwhile because the final picture showed what the assembled routes actually do: steady the eyes and adjust posture.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to connect the balance organs to the nerves was confusing because the pictures suggested a connection, but the game did not explain why it could not happen yet.

surprise.text: I expected to connect the turning sensors directly to the nerves, but the game combined the two sensor types first. Inspecting the nerves then showed a different connection was needed.

arbitrary.text: The required order for connecting the organs and nerves felt unclear. I followed the compatibility hint rather than understanding beforehand why the response routes had to be assembled separately.

continue.text: I would probably continue: seeing the separate pieces produce a recognizable response was interesting, though I would hope the next chapter makes its connection order clearer.
